subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): expose stripInboundMetadata for channel plugins

question: Should external channel plugins use a high-level SDK delivery/dispatch contract for sanitized replies, or should OpenClaw publish and support a low-level inbound-metadata sanitizer as a stable public API?
rationale: Either choice creates a long-lived plugin contract: the former establishes the intended channel ownership path, while the latter commits OpenClaw to the internal metadata grammar and its evolution.

options.title: Prefer the high-level channel contract
options.body: Confirm or extend the existing `channel-inbound` SDK seam so channel plugins receive sanitized delivery output without parsing internal prompt metadata themselves.

options.title: Publish a narrow sanitizer subpath
options.body: Add a documented non-root SDK export only if the channel dispatch seam cannot serve external plugins, with explicit stability and regression coverage for the supported behavior.

recommendation.title: Prefer the high-level channel contract
recommendation.body: Confirm or extend the existing `channel-inbound` SDK seam so channel plugins receive sanitized delivery output without parsing internal prompt metadata themselves.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent public Plugin SDK surface work provides the strongest evidence for owning the API-shape decision.
